purpose: Avatrombopag is used to raise your platelet count when it is dangerously low. It is used in adults with chronic liver disease who need a medical procedure, and also in adults with a condition called chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) when other treatments have not worked well enough. Platelets are tiny blood cells that help your blood clot and stop bleeding.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes a protein called thrombopoietin that signals your bone marrow to produce platelets. Avatrombopag works by mimicking that signal and attaching to the same receptor, telling your bone marrow to make more platelets. This helps bring your platelet count up to a safer level so you are less likely to bleed too much.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, tiredness, nausea, swelling in the hands or feet, fever, stomach pain, and bruising. Some people may also notice joint pain or feeling generally unwell.
warnings: This medication can increase your risk of blood clots, including serious clots in your veins or arteries — tell your doctor right away if you have chest pain, leg swelling, or sudden shortness of breath. Do not use it if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it may harm your baby. Your platelet count needs to be monitored regularly to avoid it going too high, which raises clot risk. Long-term use may also cause bone marrow changes over time.
typical_dosing: For liver disease patients before a procedure, the usual dose is 40 mg or 60 mg taken by mouth once daily for 5 days, starting 10 to 13 days before the procedure. For ITP, the starting dose is usually 20 mg once daily with food, and your doctor will adjust it based on your platelet count. Always take it with a meal for best absorption.
